name: kaldrax-memory-extraction-v1
description: Synthetic engineering extraction candidates with proposed expected claims. All claims are assistant-proposed and require independent human review before evaluation or release use.

cases.objective: Summarize durable storage decisions
cases.candidate: Decision: SQLite is the local durable store. The database uses write-ahead logging and a busy timeout. Rule: schema upgrades are additive and preserve existing rows. A developer also prefers dark terminal themes.

cases.objective: Extract stable API behavior
cases.candidate: Rule: retryable writes require idempotency keys. API throttling returns Retry-After. Decision: list endpoints use opaque cursors so pagination remains stable while records change.

cases.objective: Extract security controls from implementation notes
cases.candidate: Rule: session cookies use Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite. Rule: credentials and authorization headers are redacted from logs. Rule: database access uses parameterized SQL rather than string interpolation.

cases.objective: Capture resilient background processing practices
cases.candidate: Pattern: the outbox row is committed in the same transaction as the domain update. Rule: transient failures use exponential backoff with jitter. Rule: exhausted messages move to a dead-letter queue with the failure reason preserved.

cases.objective: Record observability conventions
cases.candidate: Rule: structured logs include a correlation identifier and redact personal data. Rule: trace identifiers propagate into background jobs. Decision: alert on service-level objective burn rate rather than host CPU alone.

cases.objective: Extract release and deployment safeguards
cases.candidate: Rule: readiness checks fail when a required dependency is unavailable. Rule: a failed post-deploy health check triggers rollback to the previous artifact. CI pins the Python runtime and uses the dependency lock file.

cases.objective: Summarize accessibility requirements
cases.candidate: Rule: all interactive controls work with keyboard navigation and show visible focus. Rule: text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Status must not be communicated by color alone.

cases.objective: Extract repeatable software quality practices
cases.candidate: Pattern: property-based tests exercise parser invariants over generated inputs. Rule: migration tests include the oldest supported database schema. CI runs formatting, lint, type checking, and static analysis.

cases.objective: Capture operational safety practices
cases.candidate: Rule: restore drills verify that backups are recoverable. Rule: risky launches use feature flags with an emergency kill switch. Rule: service containers run as a non-root user.

cases.objective: Extract architectural boundaries and configuration safety
cases.candidate: Decision: domain workflows depend on stable ports while provider integrations remain replaceable adapters. Rule: all memory reads are isolated by project identifier. Rule: required configuration is type-checked at startup and errors do not reveal secret values.

cases.objective: Capture database connection limits and checkout behavior
cases.candidate: Rule: PostgreSQL connections are pooled with a maximum size of 20. Rule: connection checkout timeout is capped at 2 seconds.

cases.objective: Extract transaction isolation and retry policy
cases.candidate: Decision: ledger writes use SERIALIZABLE transaction isolation. Rule: serialization failures retry at most three times with randomized backoff.

cases.objective: Record backup encryption and integrity verification
cases.candidate: Rule: database backup snapshots are encrypted with the platform key-management service. Rule: restore jobs verify the snapshot SHA-256 checksum before importing data.

cases.objective: Capture message delivery and consumer idempotency guarantees
cases.candidate: Decision: the job queue provides at-least-once message delivery. Rule: every consumer handler uses an idempotency key to prevent duplicate side effects.

cases.objective: Extract event envelope versioning and forwarding behavior
cases.candidate: Rule: every event envelope contains a schema version and producer identifier. Rule: forwarders preserve unknown optional fields for compatibility with newer producers.

cases.objective: Record access-token expiry and refresh-token rotation
cases.candidate: Rule: access tokens expire after 15 minutes. Rule: refresh tokens rotate after every successful use and the previous token is revoked.

cases.objective: Capture tenant identity and query scoping rules
cases.candidate: Rule: tenant identifiers are derived from the authenticated principal, never from an untrusted request parameter. Rule: every database query includes an explicit tenant-scoping predicate.

cases.objective: Extract credential rotation cadence and overlap window
cases.candidate: Policy: API credentials rotate every 90 days. Rule: old and new credentials overlap for no more than 24 hours during planned rotation.

cases.objective: Capture request throttling algorithm and response metadata
cases.candidate: Rule: API throttling uses a token bucket independently for each API key. Rule: rate-limited responses return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.

cases.objective: Record public API versioning and deprecation notice
cases.candidate: Decision: versioned endpoints use an explicit /v2 path prefix. Policy: deprecated API versions receive at least six months of customer notice.

cases.objective: Extract request-schema and Unicode normalization rules
cases.candidate: Rule: JSON request validators reject unknown fields instead of silently ignoring them. Rule: input strings are normalized to Unicode NFC before validation.

cases.objective: Capture upload chunk limits and content integrity checks
cases.candidate: Rule: multipart uploads accept chunks no larger than 8 MiB. Rule: the server verifies the complete file SHA-256 digest before persisting the object.

cases.objective: Record cursor semantics and deterministic ordering
cases.candidate: Rule: search pagination uses opaque continuation cursors rather than client-generated offsets. Decision: result ordering includes the record identifier as a deterministic tie-breaker.

cases.objective: Capture response caching and mutation invalidation behavior
cases.candidate: Rule: public catalog responses use Cache-Control max-age=60 seconds. Rule: successful catalog mutations invalidate the affected tenant cache immediately.

cases.objective: Extract sensitive-field redaction and trace propagation
cases.candidate: Rule: structured logs redact Authorization headers and session cookies. Rule: background workers propagate the W3C trace context from the initiating request.

cases.objective: Record error-budget paging and lower-priority host alerts
cases.candidate: Rule: page the on-call engineer when the service error-budget burn rate crosses the critical threshold. Rule: sustained high CPU utilization creates a non-paging operational alert.

cases.objective: Capture readiness gating and graceful shutdown behavior
cases.candidate: Rule: a new service instance receives production traffic only after its readiness probe succeeds. Rule: shutdown drains active connections for 30 seconds before process exit.

cases.objective: Extract startup configuration validation and failure behavior
cases.candidate: Rule: configuration values are parsed and type-checked during application startup. Rule: a missing required configuration key causes a fail-fast error without printing secret values.

cases.objective: Capture semantic form structure and accessible validation errors
cases.candidate: Rule: application forms use native semantic HTML controls with programmatic labels. Rule: inline validation messages are associated with inputs through aria-describedby.

cases.objective: Record property-based parser testing and deterministic time control
cases.candidate: Pattern: property-based tests generate malformed and valid parser inputs to exercise invariants. Rule: expiration tests inject a fake clock instead of reading wall-clock time.

candidate_expansion.note: The corpus has 30 cases and 70 proposed expected claims. Case counts and claim coverage do not establish label correctness; review every case and claim before use.
